entities.summary: King Nan of Zhou, personal name Ji Yan, was the last king of the Zhou dynasty of China, ruling from 314 BC until his death in 256 BC. He was the son of King Shenjing and grandson of King Xian, and his 59-year reign was the longest in the Zhou dynasty and all of pre-imperial China. Nan's reign was marked by significant cultural and political developments, including the introduction of the first standardized weights and measures system and the promotion of Confucianism as the state philosophy. Despite his long and stable reign, Nan's dynasty ultimately faced significant challenges, including internal power struggles and external threats from neighboring states. His legacy continued to shape Chinese politics and society for centuries after his death, with many later dynasties emulating his policies and reforms. The fall of the Zhou dynasty marked the beginning of a period of significant change and upheaval in Chinese history, setting the stage for the rise of the Qin dynasty and the eventual establishment of the imperial system.
